datasets.title: Myanmar Earthquake: Mandalay Building Damage Assessment
datasets.description: Microsoft AI for Good Lab ran their damage assessment AI models on images provided by Planet and have mapped out the affected buildings in Mandalay, Myanmar.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/myanmar-earthquake-building-damage-assessment-from-3-28-2025]
datasets.details: While the data provides a valuable first look, it should serve as a preliminary guide and will require on-the-ground verification for a complete understanding.

lineage.description: Microsoft AI for Good Lab applied trained damage assessment models to Planet SkySat satellite imagery acquired on 29 March 2025 over Mandalay, Myanmar to automatically detect and classify earthquake-damaged buildings, producing a vector dataset of affected building footprints with damage predictions.

sources.name: Planet

sources.name: Microsoft AI for Good Lab
sources.description: Deep learning damage assessment model applied to satellite imagery to classify building damage states

resources.title: skysat_20250329_080228_predictions_merged.gpkg
resources.description: The images cover Mandalay, Myanmar. Analysis was done on Planet imagery captured 03/28/2025. -180,004 buildings with damage fraction between 0% and 20% -709 buildings with damage fraction between 20% and 40% -456 buildings with damage fraction between 40% and 60% -359 buildings with damage fraction between 60% and 80% -515 buildings with damage fraction between 80% and 100% The result file contains the following fields for each building footprint: -damage_pct_0m - the fraction of the building footprint's area that is classified as damaged by our model -damaged - 1 if damage_pct_0m > 0 else 0 -unknown_pct - fraction of the pixels within the building footprint that we think are obstructed (clouds, smoke, haze, too dark to evaluate)
